name: MonarchStatusDot
title: StatusDot
summary: A small coloured dot followed by a text label, such as "Running", in five tones and two sizes, with an optional pulse.
whenToUse: To show the state of an item in a dense place such as a list row or a table cell, where a badge is too heavy.
whenNotToUse: For a status that should stand out, use MonarchBadge. Do not use the dot without words: with isLabelHidden, show a legend near it.
api: init(_ label: String, tone: MonarchTone = .neutral, size: MonarchStatusDotSize = .sm, isPulsing: Bool = false, isLabelHidden: Bool = false)

options.name: label
options.description: The words for the status, already localised.

options.name: tone
options.description: neutral, info, success, warning or danger. Selects the colour of the dot.

options.name: size
options.description: sm is an 8-point dot with caption text, md a 10-point dot with label text.

options.name: isPulsing
options.description: A ring pulses around the dot, for something live or in progress.

options.name: isLabelHidden
options.description: The label is not drawn but is still read by VoiceOver.

states.name: pulsing
states.description: A ring of the dot's colour grows from the dot and fades, repeatedly. It is not drawn when Reduce Motion is on.

states.name: label hidden
states.description: Only the dot is drawn; VoiceOver still reads the label.

appearance: The dot is filled with the solid colour of the tone, or the subtle text colour for the neutral tone; the label uses the default text colour. The roles resolve per theme, including the two high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web StatusDot also has an accent tone. MonarchTone has no accent case, so iOS offers five tones, not six. The web hides the label with a visually-hidden class; iOS does not draw it and sets it as the accessibility label. Android has the same name and parameters.
accessibility: The dot and the label are one element, read as the label.
The dot and the pulse are decorative; the meaning is in the words.
The pulse does not run when Reduce Motion is on.
The dot and the text scale with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: A long label wraps; the dot stays on the first line.
With isLabelHidden, sighted people see only colour, so pair it with a legend.
With Reduce Motion on, a pulsing dot looks the same as a still one.

examples.title: Tones
examples.template:
MonarchFlowLayout(spacing: MonarchTokens.Space.space3, rowSpacing: MonarchTokens.Space.space2) {
    MonarchStatusDot({{items.0.label}}, tone: {{items.0.tone|tone}})
    MonarchStatusDot({{items.1.label}}, tone: {{items.1.tone|tone}})
    MonarchStatusDot({{items.2.label}}, tone: {{items.2.tone|tone}})
    MonarchStatusDot({{items.3.label}}, tone: {{items.3.tone|tone}})
    MonarchStatusDot({{items.4.label}}, tone: {{items.4.tone|tone}})
    MonarchStatusDot({{items.5.label}}, tone: {{items.5.tone|tone}})
}
examples.code:
MonarchFlowLayout(spacing: MonarchTokens.Space.space3, rowSpacing: MonarchTokens.Space.space2) {
    MonarchStatusDot("Draft", tone: .neutral)
    MonarchStatusDot("Scheduled", tone: .info)
    MonarchStatusDot("Running", tone: .success)
    MonarchStatusDot("Paused", tone: .warning)
    MonarchStatusDot("Failed", tone: .danger)
    MonarchStatusDot("Featured", tone: .accent)
}
